     7	
     8	# Reading Uploaded Files
     9	
    10	## Why this skill exists
    11	
    12	When a user uploads a file in claude.ai, Claude Desktop, or Cowork,
    13	the file is written to `/mnt/user-data/uploads/<filename>` and you are told the path
    14	in an `<uploaded_files>` block. **The content is not in your context.**
    15	You must go read it.
    16	
    17	The naive thing — `cat /mnt/user-data/uploads/whatever` — is wrong for
    18	most files:
    19	
    20	- On a PDF it prints binary garbage.
    21	- On a 100MB CSV it floods your context with rows you will never use.
    22	- On a DOCX it prints the raw ZIP bytes.
    23	- On an image it does nothing useful at all.
    24	
    25	This skill tells you the right first move for each type, and when to
    26	hand off to a deeper skill.
    27	
    28	## General protocol
    29	
    30	1. **Look at the extension.** That is your dispatch key.
    31	2. **Stat before you read.** Large files need sampling, not slurping.
    32	   ```bash
    33	   stat -c '%s bytes, %y' /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    34	   file /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    35	   ```
    36	3. **Read just enough to answer the user's question.** If they asked
    37	   "how many rows are in this CSV", don't load the whole thing into
    38	   pandas — `wc -l` gives a fast approximation (it counts newlines,
    39	   not CSV records, so it may over-count if quoted fields contain
    40	   embedded newlines).
    41	4. **If a dedicated skill exists, go read it.** The table below tells

Cloud Archive Setup Guide

The Braided Mind can sync its identity and memories to cloud storage for long-term persistence. This enables:

  • Disaster recovery - Restore your AI if hardware fails
  • Cross-device sync - Access the same identity from multiple machines
  • Long-term archival - Memories persist indefinitely

Free Tier Options

Option 1: Cloudflare R2 (Recommended)

  • Free: 10GB storage, no egress fees
  • Cost: $0 beyond free tier
  • Sign up: https://dash.cloudflare.com/sign-up/r2

Option 2: Backblaze B2

  • Free: 10GB storage
  • Egress: First 1GB/day free
  • Sign up: https://www.backblaze.com/b2/sign-up.html

Option 3: AWS S3

  • Free: 5GB for 12 months (AWS Free Tier)
  • Note: Egress fees apply
  • Sign up: https://aws.amazon.com/free

Setup Instructions (Cloudflare R2)

Step 1: Create R2 Bucket

  1. Go to https://dash.cloudflare.com
  2. Navigate to R2 Object Storage
  3. Click "Create bucket"
  4. Name it something like braided-mind-archive
  5. Choose a location close to you

Step 2: Create API Token

  1. In R2, go to "Manage R2 API Tokens"
  2. Click "Create API token"
  3. Settings:
    • Name: braided-mind-token
    • Permissions: Object Read & Write
    • TTL: Leave blank (no expiration)
  4. Click "Create API Token"
  5. Copy these values (shown only once!):
    • Access Key ID
    • Secret Access Key
    • Endpoint URL (looks like: https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com)

Step 3: Configure Environment

Create or edit .env file in your braided_mind directory:

# Hugging Face Token
HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN=your_hf_token_here

# Cloud Archive Configuration
ARCHIVE_BUCKET=braided-mind-archive
ARCHIVE_ENDPOINT=https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
ARCHIVE_ACCESS_KEY=your_access_key_id
ARCHIVE_SECRET_KEY=your_secret_access_key
ARCHIVE_REGION=auto

# Optional: Encryption key (generate your own)
# Run: python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"
ARCHIVE_ENCRYPTION_KEY=your_generated_encryption_key

Step 4: Test Connection

python main.py
# At the prompt:
status
# Check that cloud archive shows "connected: True"

Setup Instructions (Backblaze B2)

Step 1: Create Bucket

  1. Go to https://www.backblaze.com/b2/buckets.html
  2. Click "Create a Bucket"
  3. Name: braided-mind-archive
  4. Keep defaults, create

Step 2: Create Application Key

  1. Go to App Keys under Account
  2. Click "Add a New Application Key"
  3. Name: braided-mind-key
  4. Allow access to specific bucket: braided-mind-archive
  5. Access: Read and Write
  6. Create and copy:
    • keyID (Access Key)
    • applicationKey (Secret Key)

Step 3: Configure

ARCHIVE_BUCKET=braided-mind-archive
ARCHIVE_ENDPOINT=https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com  # Use your bucket's endpoint
ARCHIVE_ACCESS_KEY=your_key_id
ARCHIVE_SECRET_KEY=your_application_key

Usage

Once configured, use these commands:

# Sync identity and memories to cloud
sync

# Create full backup snapshot
backup

# Restore from cloud archive
restore

What Gets Archived

Always Synced

  • Identity State - Your core self, goals, focus, thought count
  • Recent Memories - Significant learnings and experiences

On Backup

  • Full Snapshot - Complete state including constitution
  • All Memories - Everything stored in the library

Storage Estimates

Content Size Estimate
Identity state ~10 KB
100 memories ~50 KB
1000 memories ~500 KB
Full snapshot ~1-5 MB

With 10GB free storage, you can store:

  • ~200,000 memories
  • ~2,000 full snapshots

Security Notes

  1. Encryption: If you set ARCHIVE_ENCRYPTION_KEY, all data is encrypted before upload
  2. Access Keys: Never commit .env to git or share publicly
  3. Bucket Privacy: Keep buckets private (default setting)

Troubleshooting

"Cloud archive not configured"

  • Check that all ARCHIVE_* environment variables are set
  • Restart the system after updating .env

"Connection refused" / "Access Denied"

  • Verify Access Key and Secret Key are correct
  • Check bucket name matches exactly
  • Verify endpoint URL is correct for your provider

"Sync failed"

  • Check internet connection
  • Verify bucket permissions (Read/Write)
  • Check Cloudflare/Backblaze status pages

Cross-Device Setup

To use the same identity on multiple machines:

  1. Set up Braided Mind on both machines
  2. Configure the same cloud archive on both
  3. On the first machine: run sync
  4. On the second machine: run restore
  5. Both now share the same identity and memories

Note: Sync is not automatic. Remember to sync before switching machines.

Cloud Archive Setup Guide

The Braided Mind can sync its identity and memories to cloud storage for long-term persistence. This enables:

  • Disaster recovery - Restore your AI if hardware fails
  • Cross-device sync - Access the same identity from multiple machines
  • Long-term archival - Memories persist indefinitely

Free Tier Options

Option 1: Cloudflare R2 (Recommended)

  • Free: 10GB storage, no egress fees
  • Cost: $0 beyond free tier
  • Sign up: https://dash.cloudflare.com/sign-up/r2

Option 2: Backblaze B2

  • Free: 10GB storage
  • Egress: First 1GB/day free
  • Sign up: https://www.backblaze.com/b2/sign-up.html

Option 3: AWS S3

  • Free: 5GB for 12 months (AWS Free Tier)
  • Note: Egress fees apply
  • Sign up: https://aws.amazon.com/free

Setup Instructions (Cloudflare R2)

Step 1: Create R2 Bucket

  1. Go to https://dash.cloudflare.com
  2. Navigate to R2 Object Storage
  3. Click "Create bucket"
  4. Name it something like braided-mind-archive
  5. Choose a location close to you

Step 2: Create API Token

  1. In R2, go to "Manage R2 API Tokens"
  2. Click "Create API token"
  3. Settings:
    • Name: braided-mind-token
    • Permissions: Object Read & Write
    • TTL: Leave blank (no expiration)
  4. Click "Create API Token"
  5. Copy these values (shown only once!):
    • Access Key ID
    • Secret Access Key
    • Endpoint URL (looks like: https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com)

Step 3: Configure Environment

Create or edit .env file in your braided_mind directory:

# Hugging Face Token

  • Check that all ARCHIVE_* environment variables are set
  • Restart the system after updating .env

  • Verify Access Key and Secret Key are correct
  • Check bucket name matches exactly
  • Verify endpoint URL is correct for your provider

  • Check internet connection
  • Verify bucket permissions (Read/Write)
  • Check Cloudflare/Backblaze status pages

  1. Set up Braided Mind on both machines
  2. Configure the same cloud archive on both
  3. On the first machine: run sync
  4. On the second machine: run restore
  5. Both now share the same identity and memories
